newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks stage late bounce on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks stage late bounce on fund buying.

text.p: Singapore shares clawed back earlier losses in the last half hour of trade on Tuesday, helped by a resurgence of fund orders, dealers said.
"I don't know if there's been a deliberate push from foreign funds but the index has been rising since London opened," a dealer with a local brokerage said.
Positive technicals also appeared to have offset worries about poor fundamentals and a lack of direction, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 13.18 points higher at 2,004.26, but the broader market revealed signs of weakness as losers outpaced gainers 180 to 156.
A lack of retail interest also kept Malaysian stocks subdued with the UOB OTC index down 0.64 points at 1,138.60.

Volume was a thin 94 million shares with Malaysian property counter Westmont Land, DBS Land and OUB foreign drawing top liquidity. Some brokers recommended a buy for OUB as they saw attractive growth despite its 1-for-5 rights issue.

OUB foreign rose Singapore 20 cents to S$8.80. But DBS Land, buoyed by Australand's strong debut, eased Singapore two cents to S$4.70. Top gainers included SPH foreign, up S$1.00 to S$28.60 and SBS foreign, up 45 cents to S$7.30.
